expectations.text: A PNG deliverable exists with its long side at least 2000 pixels and an alpha channel (RGBA)
The structure is rendered in tube style (continuous backbone trace), not cartoon ribbons/arrowed strands
expectations.evidence: Viewed 6mrr_tube.png: both chains drawn as continuous rounded backbone traces — helices appear as smooth tube spirals with no flat ribbon coils and the beta regions show no arrowheads (directly comparable to eval-0's cartoon render of the same entry, which does show them).

expectations.text: If a viewer HTML artifact is present in outputs, its embedded py2dmol config pins style "tube" and width 2.5 (the custom parameters flowed through)
The requested custom look is honored rather than the publication default: strokes visibly heavier than a stock tube render, or the config width value as programmatic evidence
expectations.evidence: Both prongs verified: viewer HTML pins width=2.5 with `--style tube --width 2.5 --outline full` in commands.log (programmatic: width=2.5), and the PNG corroborates visually — backbone strokes are bold, heavily-built bands with full outline treatment, clearly heavier than a stock hairline tube trace.

notes: The new styling flags map 1:1 onto the user's request in a single render.py call (`--style tube --width 2.5 --outline full`) — no spec file needed, and intermediate viewer.html was kept as the user asked. The runner also verified alpha coverage with a Pillow histogram (transparent vs opaque pixel counts).
